![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/d3d0f871d60b7f7c8280abd7d3eba4337f910bae6b814586b368bbfb0a8dc313.png)

The scatter plot above shows the weight loss per week (in pounds) vs. the number of hours spent training per week for a group of people. Use the trend line to estimate how much weight a person loses if they train for $4$ hours per week.
question.worked_solution:
To make our estimation, we proceed as follows:

- We start at $x=4$ on the horizontal axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/1e397473de815e2eda88ad33c59e2cf77c336b968ef6a1eeaffa67d9fbc64750.png)

- Then, we move up until we intersect the trend line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/27c8ce8a7a1feadd4ea16d66f6a283fa245fa737036810924ead4b0148c6d6f5.png)

- Finally, we move left until we intersect the vertical axis.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14227574/assets/a178070d1f62538a35e7e4e363a254c2afa776920079618b80b3bff358601871.png)

Therefore, a person training $4$ hours a week will lose around $3$ pounds of weight.
